text: Is GSE309890 the same thing as GDS309890?

Abstract
GSE309890 (Series) and GDS309890 (DataSet) are both GEO entries associated with the same general study footprint but represent different GEO record types. To assess whether they are “the same thing,” we queried GEO for GSE309890 and GDS309890 using dedicated tools. GSE309890 is a Series entry with 6 samples (GSMs), produced by Escherichia coli K-12 substr. MG1655, on platform GPL24659, date public 2026-02-01, Bioproject PRJNA1363958, and an FTP directory path for the series. It has no linked PubMed record. The corresponding dataset-oriented entry GDS309890 exists as a separate DataSet entry with its own FTP directory and GEO page, and is identified by UID 309890 in the GDS namespace. However, the two records have distinct accession identifiers, record types, and likely distinct internal indexing, indicating they are not the same record. They may reflect related components of the same overall study metadata (e.g., linked via a Bioproject), but are separate GEO records. Key numerical outputs used in this comparison come directly from the GEO queries: (i) GSE309890: 6 samples, six GSMs listed, taxon, platform, and Bioproject; (ii) GDS309890: separate dataset entry with its own FTP and GEO links. This distinction matters for data provenance and downstream retrieval.

I. Introduction
Background. The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) catalogs gene expression data as multiple record types, notably Series (GSE) and DataSet (GDS). Understanding whether two accession numbers represent the same underlying data is essential for reproducibility and data merging.
Literature Review. No PubMed records were retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. It was unclear whether GSE309890 and GDS309890 refer to the same data object or to distinct GEO records that may be interlinked.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: determine whether GSE309890 and GDS309890 are the same dataset. Hypothesis: they are distinct GEO records (Series vs DataSet) that may pertain to the same study footprint but cannot be treated as identical data entries.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. Retrieval of GEO entries for GSE309890 and GDS309890 to compare record type, contents, and cross-links.
Materials. Tools: GEO series resolver and GEO dataset resolver.
Procedures. 
- Tool call 1: GEO series resolver with accession = "GSE309890", list_files = false.
  - Extracted fields: accession, uid, entry_type, entry_type_label, title, taxon, platform, date_public, sample_count, samples, bioproject, pubmed_ids, pubmed_note, ftp_directory_url, supplementary_file_types, geo_url, expression_values, and api_call.
- Tool call 2: GEO dataset resolver with accession = "GDS309890".
  - Extracted fields: accession, uid, entry_type, ftp_directory_url, geo_url.
- Comparison: Assess whether the two records share identical data objects, noting that one is a Series (GSE) and the other is a DataSet (GDS). Look for cross-references (e.g., Bioproject), overlapping publication status, and distinct identifiers.

Statistical Analysis. Descriptive comparison of record-type, sample counts, organism, platform, and access URLs derived directly from the tool outputs. All numbers come from the tool-reported fields and are not inferred.

III. Results
Data Presentation

Table 1. GEO entries retrieved and key attributes
- GSE309890 (Series)
  - Type: GSE (Series)
  - Title: Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback
  - Taxon: Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655
  - Experiment type: Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing
  - Date public: 2026/02/01
  - Platform: GPL24659
  - Sample count: 6
  - Samples: GSM9284462; GSM9284459; GSM9284457; GSM9284460; GSM9284461; GSM9284458
  - Bioproject: PRJNA1363958
  - PubMed: None linked
  - ftp_directory_url: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
  - geo_url: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
- GDS309890 (DataSet)
  - Type: GDS (DataSet)
  - uid: 309890
  - ftp_directory_url: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/
  - geo_url: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890

Findings. 
- GSE309890 is a Series (GSE) record with 6 samples in Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655, associated with PRJNA1363958, and includes a dedicated Series FTP directory and a GEO page. It does not show a linked PubMed record according to retrieved data.
- GDS309890 is a separate DataSet (GDS) record with its own GEO page and dedicated Dataset FTP directory.
- The two records have different accession identifiers and record types, indicating they are not the same GEO record. There is no PubMed linkage reported for either in the retrieved data, and no explicit single-object merge visible in the retrieved fields.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The retrieved data demonstrate that GSE309890 and GDS309890 are distinct GEO entries (Series vs DataSet) with separate identifiers and storage locations, not the same single record. They may reflect related study metadata (e.g., same Bioproject PRJNA1363958) but are not interchangeable as identical data objects.
Context. The existence of both records aligns with GEO’s historical practice of maintaining multiple record types for related data. The GSE record provides sample-level metadata (GSMs) under a Series umbrella, while the GDS record represents a separate Dataset entity in GEO’s older schema.
Limitations. The retrieved records do not show a direct one-to-one mapping or explicit cross-linking within the returned fields. PubMed linkage is absent in both entries, limiting conclusive linkage to literature references. The data presented are metadata-level; processed expression values are not accessible via these endpoints.
Conclusion & Future Directions. GSE309890 and GDS309890 are not the same GEO record; they are distinct entries representing different GEO record types. If a user requires unified data retrieval, consider querying both records and cross-referencing Bioproject/PRJNA entries, or exploring any GEO-linked supplementary files to understand potential overlaps. If needed, we can attempt to locate any explicit cross-links (e.g., GEO series to GEO dataset) beyond the current results.

[2] NCBI GEO. GSE309nnn/GSE309890 FTP directory. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[3] NCBI GEO. GDS309890 page. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890
[4] NCBI GEO. GDS309nnn/GDS309890 FTP directory. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/
